about.title: Garden Grove Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Work in Garden Grove takes many forms: warehouse shifts, restaurant kitchens along Garden Grove Boulevard, construction crews, delivery routes that thread SR-22 and Brookhurst Street. When a shift ends with an injury, the path forward usually starts with workers' compensation. In California, that system is generally your only remedy against your employer, and it pays regardless of who was at fault. But it is not always the whole story. If a subcontractor, a property owner, an equipment manufacturer, or another driver caused the harm, a separate injury claim against that third party may be available, and it runs on a two-year clock. Employees who drive for work should know that Garden Grove recorded 623 injury collisions in 2025, with reported crashes tending to cluster on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects injured Orange County workers with an independent attorney who can sort out which claims apply. Report your injury to your employer within 30 days; retaliation for doing so is illegal.

whyChoose.title: Why Garden Grove Workers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Two Systems, One Clear Explanation
items.desc: Workers' compensation covers you regardless of fault, but it is usually your only route against your employer. The attorney we connect you with can explain where that system stops and whether a third-party claim begins.

items.title: Third-Party Claims Are Easy to Miss
items.desc: A subcontractor, a property owner, an equipment maker, or another driver on SR-22 may bear responsibility beyond what workers' comp pays. Those claims carry a two-year deadline, so an early review matters.

items.title: Your Job Is Protected When You Report
items.desc: California requires you to notify your employer within 30 days, and it makes retaliation for reporting illegal. An independent attorney can help you document the report and respond if your employer pushes back.

items.question: I was hurt driving for work on Garden Grove Boulevard. Is that a workers' comp case or a car accident case?
items.answer: It can be both. If you were on the clock, workers' compensation generally applies no matter who caused the collision. If another driver was at fault, you may also have a separate third-party injury claim against that driver, which follows California's two-year deadline. An attorney can review the police report and your work status to see which paths are open.

items.question: Can my Garden Grove employer fire me for filing a workers' compensation claim?
items.answer: No. California law prohibits employers from retaliating against workers who report an injury or file a claim. You should still report the injury within 30 days to protect your rights. If you experience demotion, reduced hours, or termination after reporting, tell the attorney you are connected with right away.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm, and we do not handle your case ourselves. We connect Orange County workers with an independent personal injury attorney who works on contingency, meaning there is no attorney fee unless there is a recovery. You decide whether to move forward after that first conversation.
